title: How to Prequalify Borrowers Without a Hard Pull
summary: Learn how US lenders and embedded-finance platforms can prequalify consumer and SMB borrowers with soft inquiries, permissioned bank data, and business credit files. This guide covers FCRA permissible purpose, Reg B inquiry rules, and a seven-step workflow that saves the hard pull for the formal application.
body_markdown:
To prequalify borrowers without a hard pull, combine self-reported intake, an authorized soft inquiry, permissioned cash-flow data, and business credit files. Save the hard pull for the formal application. When your team initiates the outreach instead of the borrower, a prescreened firm offer is the soft-pull route the FCRA provides.


That sequence matters because a hard inquiry at the top of the funnel adds friction before a borrower knows what they could qualify for. Lendflow reports[$1.5B+ in capital funded](https://www.lendflow.com/lendflow-connect) through Connect-powered programs, and its[Automate](https://www.lendflow.com/lendflow-automate) Voice AI and Chatbot agents report a 42% quicker funding cycle.


This guide covers the data behind no-hard-pull prequalification, the federal rules that keep it an inquiry, and a workflow for consumer and SMB lending. It reflects US federal law only and is not legal advice, so review your flow with counsel before launch.


‍


### Why Soft-Pull Prequalification Protects Conversion


A soft-pull prequalification step lets a borrower see likely terms before committing to a full application. For lenders and embedded-finance platforms, it keeps early-funnel shoppers moving while reserving the hard inquiry for borrowers who choose to apply.


#### Hard Inquiries vs. Soft Inquiries


The CFPB explains that hard inquiries[can impact credit scores](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-credit-inquiry-en-1317/) because most scoring models weigh how recently and often a person applies. The same page says soft inquiries, including prescreening by prospective lenders, don't affect scores and are shown only to the consumer.


The cost of a hard pull is real but modest for most people. According to[myFICO](https://www.myfico.com/credit-education/blog/rate-shop) , one additional hard inquiry costs fewer than five FICO points for most people, although there is no set number. FICO also notes that hard inquiries can stay on a report for up to 24 months, while FICO Scores only consider them for 12 months.


The bigger issue for personal and SMB lenders is rate shopping. FICO groups mortgage, auto, and student loan inquiries into one window: 14 days on older score versions and 45 days on newer ones. Because FICO versions vary by lender, the window a borrower gets depends on the score used.


FICO applies this treatment only to mortgage, auto, and student loan inquiries. Borrowers who compare other types of credit through hard pulls may collect multiple inquiries.


#### Prequalification vs. Preapproval


Lenders use these labels loosely, so the regulatory definition is more useful than the marketing one. Under[Reg B comment 2(f)-5](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/Interp-2) , preapproval means a comprehensive creditworthiness analysis plus a written commitment to lend up to a set amount for a set period.


That makes a preapproval request an application. If a program offers no written commitments, Reg B treats preapproval requests as prequalification requests, so program design decides the category rather than the label.


‍


### The Data Sources That Replace an Early Hard Pull


No single input replaces a full credit review, but several sources together can produce a credible prequalified offer. The right mix depends on whether you lend to consumers, to businesses, or to businesses backed by personal guarantors.


#### Self-Reported Intake


Self-reported income, revenue, time in business, industry, and requested amount give your decision rules a starting point at no bureau cost. Treat these fields as unverified inputs that set a likely range, then confirm them with documents or data at application.


#### Soft Inquiries With Written Authorization


A soft inquiry still requires a permissible purpose, and the clearest one is the consumer's own request.[FCRA §604(a)(2)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/1681b) allows a credit bureau to furnish a report in accordance with the written instructions of the consumer it relates to.


The CFPB's consumer guidance lists prescreening and existing-account reviews as soft inquiries, but it does not address consumer-authorized prequal pulls specifically. Confirm with your bureau that your prequal product posts as a soft inquiry before you promise borrowers it won't affect their score.


#### Permissioned Cash-Flow and Bank Data


Bank transaction data, shared with the borrower's permission, adds a view of revenue, balances, and obligations that a credit file can miss. A June 2025[FinRegLab and NYU Stern study](https://finreglab.org/research/sharpening-the-focus-using-cash-flow-data-to-underwrite-financially-constrained-businesses/) analyzed[more than 38,000 small business loans](https://finreglab.org/press-releases/finreglab-study-shows-cash-flow-data-can-expand-small-business-lending/) from two fintech lenders. Adding cash-flow data substantially increased the predictive signal of models built mainly on owners' personal scores.


The effect was larger for low-score owners of businesses under five years old, a segment many prequal flows screen out early.


The study covers two small business lenders and was funded in part by Visa. Treat it as directional evidence for SMB underwriting rather than proof for consumer prequal.


On the regulatory side, consumer-permissioned data sharing operates commercially, but the CFPB's open banking rule is not in force. In October 2025, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Kentucky enjoined the CFPB from enforcing the 12 CFR 1033 rule until it completes its reconsideration ([Forcht Bank, N.A. v. CFPB, order of Oct. 29, 2025](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.kyed.106299/gov.uscourts.kyed.106299.90.0_3.pdf) ). The CFPB's[August 2026 regulatory agenda (91 FR 53082)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/08/14/2026-16613.txt) lists a rulemaking to reconsider the rule, so recheck its status before you build around it.


#### Business Credit Files and Owner Reports


For SMB lending, reports on the business entity from commercial bureaus generally fall outside the FCRA. An informal[FTC staff opinion from 2000](https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/advisory-opinions/advisory-opinion-tatelbaum-07-26-00) states that business-history information collected by a commercial reporting agency for business transactions is not a consumer report.


Personal reports on owners and guarantors are a different matter. The same FTC staff opinion says a report on an individual stays a consumer report. When the business is the applicant, the individual's written authorization is the lender's dependable permissible purpose.


#### Prescreened Firm Offers


Prescreening is the lender-initiated route, where a bureau provides a list of consumers who meet your criteria. Under[FCRA §604(c)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/1681b) , a prescreen requires a firm offer of credit and must exclude consumers who have opted out.


‍


### The Compliance Lines That Keep Prequal an Inquiry


A soft pull changes the borrower's score impact, but it does not remove your obligations under the FCRA or ECOA. The rules below are where most no-hard-pull flows succeed or fail.


#### FCRA Permissible Purpose


Every consumer report, soft or hard, needs a permissible purpose. FCRA §604(a)(3)(A) covers reports used in connection with a credit transaction involving the consumer. The statute text doesn't settle whether that reaches a prequal request that never becomes an application, so written instructions are the clearer basis.


Whether a click-through or e-signed consent satisfies the "written instructions" standard is a question for counsel. Capture the consent language, timestamp, and version with every pull so you can show what the borrower agreed to.


#### Reg B: When an Inquiry Becomes an Application


Reg B decides whether a prequal request is an inquiry or an application based on how the creditor responds. Under[comment 2(f)-3](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/Interp-2) , a creditor that evaluates the consumer, decides to decline, and communicates that decision has received an application. At that point, §1002.9 notice requirements apply.


[Comment 9-5](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/interp-9/) draws the other side of the line. A creditor may treat the request as an inquiry when it shares the amount, rate, and terms the consumer could qualify for.


That makes the no-offer screen the riskiest page in the flow, so have counsel review its wording and routing. If a prequal decline does become an application, ECOA and the FCRA each require their own disclosures. Reg B[comment 9(b)(2)-9](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/interp-9/) notes that disclosing a credit report was used in a denial does not satisfy the ECOA duty to give specific reasons.


#### Prescreen Opt-Outs and Firm Offers


Consumers can block prescreened offers through the bureau system. The[FTC explains](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/what-know-about-prescreened-offers-credit-and-insurance) that consumers can opt out for five years at optoutprescreen.com or 1-888-5-OPT-OUT, or permanently with a signed form.


Mortgage lenders face an added limit.[Pub. L. 119-36](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/15/1681b) , enacted September 5, 2025, added FCRA §604(c)(4), which restricts prescreen lists built from residential mortgage inquiries starting 180 days after enactment.


#### Business Borrowers vs. Personal Guarantors


Reg B applies to business credit as well as consumer credit, and[comment 9(a)(3)-4](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1002/interp-9/) notes that business creditors may follow the consumer notification rules. The inquiry-versus-application line therefore applies to SMB prequal too, with notice timing that varies by the business's revenue.


When the business is the applicant, the FTC staff opinion says the credit-transaction purpose gives no authority to pull a guarantor's or co-signer's report. Collect written authorization from each owner or guarantor whose personal file you plan to review.

### How to Prequalify Borrowers Without a Hard Pull in Seven Steps


The workflow below fits consumer and SMB products delivered through widgets, landing pages, or APIs. Adjust each step to your product, state footprint, and counsel's guidance.


#### Step 1: Define What Prequal Can Promise


Decide whether your prequal output is an estimated range, a list of products the borrower may qualify for, or a firm offer from a prescreen. Write that definition down, because Reg B classifies the request by how you respond, and your product, legal, and design teams need the same answer.


#### Step 2: Collect Self-Reported Intake First


Ask for the minimum fields your rules need, such as revenue, time in business, industry, and amount requested. Use these inputs to route borrowers to likely products before you spend on any bureau or data call.


#### Step 3: Capture Written Authorization Before Any Pull


Present clear consent language for each individual whose consumer report you will request, including owners and guarantors in SMB flows. Store the consent text, version, and timestamp alongside the application record.


#### Step 4: Run Soft Inquiries and Business Credit Files


Request the soft-pull product your bureau has confirmed posts as a soft inquiry, and pull commercial bureau files on the business entity. Keep consumer and commercial data separate in your records, since different rules govern each.


#### Step 5: Add Permissioned Bank Data Where It Changes the Answer


Invite borrowers to connect bank accounts when cash flow would change their result, such as thin-file owners or young businesses. Limit collection and retention to what the borrower's requested product needs.


#### Step 6: Present Terms, Not Declines


Show the amounts, rates, and products the borrower may qualify for. Route borrowers who miss your criteria to a second-look waterfall where other lenders can review the deal. For anyone without a match, have counsel approve the no-offer screen so it doesn't communicate a decline.


#### Step 7: Reserve the Hard Pull for the Formal Application


Tell the borrower before submission that applying triggers a hard inquiry, then run it only after they choose to proceed. At this stage, verify intake against documents and complete full underwriting and any adverse-action notices.


‍


### Best Practices and Common Pitfalls for Soft-Pull Prequal


A well-built prequal flow is clear with borrowers about what each step does to their credit. These practices keep the experience fast and the record defensible.


- Label every credit check with its type, and say "won't affect your credit score" only after your bureau confirms it.
- Never call a prequalified offer "approved," since Reg B ties preapproval to a written commitment program.
- Avoid "you don't qualify" language on no-offer screens, because communicating a decline can turn the request into an application.
- Collect separate authorization from each owner or guarantor, since one signer's consent doesn't cover another person's report.
- Don't assume business loans escape the FCRA, because personal reports on individuals stay consumer reports.
- Honor prescreen opt-outs and make every prescreened offer firm, or the soft-pull route loses its legal basis.
- Avoid building around the CFPB's 1033 rule as if it were in force, and recheck its status before launch.
- Version your consent text and decision rules together, so you can show what logic produced any past offer.


‍


### Prequalify Early and Pull Hard Only at Application


You can prequalify borrowers without a hard pull by combining self-reported intake, authorized soft inquiries, permissioned cash-flow data, business credit files, and prescreened firm offers. The hard inquiry belongs at the formal application, after the borrower has seen their likely terms and chosen to proceed.


The compliance work sits in three details: a permissible purpose for every report, terms instead of declines, and authorization from every guarantor. Get those right, and prequalification becomes a faster path to funding that borrowers can trust.


‍


### Frequently Asked Questions


#### Does a Soft Pull Affect a Borrower's Credit Score?


According to the[CFPB](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-credit-inquiry-en-1317/) , soft inquiries such as prescreening and account reviews do not affect credit scores and are shown only to the consumer. Confirm with your bureau that your specific prequal product posts as a soft inquiry.


#### Do I Need Consent to Run a Soft Pull for Prequalification?


You need a permissible purpose for any consumer report, soft or hard. For borrower-initiated prequal, the clearest basis is the consumer's written instructions under FCRA §604(a)(2), so collect consent and have counsel confirm your electronic method.


#### Is Prequalification Exempt From Adverse Action Notices?


No, not automatically. Under Reg B, a prequal request stays an inquiry when you share terms the borrower may qualify for. It becomes an application if you evaluate, decline, and communicate that decline.


#### Can SMB Lenders Prequalify Without Pulling the Owner's Personal Credit?


Yes, if your criteria rely on commercial bureau files, self-reported intake, and permissioned bank data. Commercial reports on the business generally fall outside the FCRA. Any personal report on an owner or guarantor is a consumer report that needs a permissible purpose.


#### What Is the Difference Between Prequalification and a Prescreened Offer?


The borrower initiates prequalification, while the lender initiates a prescreen using a bureau list. A prescreen must include a firm offer of credit and exclude consumers who opted out at optoutprescreen.com.
